thread:
Sam: Quick RFC follow-up — our console panels still fan out dozens of queries on load and that's hitting p99 SLOs. I'm proposing a refactor: introduce a small query-planner service that dedupes/batches panel queries, applies auth filter pushdown, and can return cached/stale results when under pressure. Thoughts? :eyes:
Anya: Do we have concrete numbers on how much this contributes to tail latency?
Sam: Yep — on Friday we saw dashboard X spike: panel-level p99 went from ~220ms -> ~1.05s during a traffic burst. Rough breakdown: merged/fanout queries were ~30% of extra CPU and ~40% of added latency at p99.
Kevin: Auth pushdown makes sense for cost but is a big correctness surface. If we move RBAC filtering into planner, how do we handle policy changes/invalidation?
Maria: Alternative: add an aggregator cache layer that returns precomputed panel payloads (TTL ~60s) and falls back to live queries. Lower risk but may increase storage and cache invalidation complexity.
Anya: Tradeoffs: precomputed payloads reduce compute on peak but add write amplification and more infra to keep per-tenant scoping correct. Also sensitive panels require stricter cache policies.
Kevin: If we do pushdown, we need a revocable auth cache keyed by user-session + policy-hash. On policy change we increment the hash to force recalculation.
Sam: Sketch of planner flow: ```
// pseudo
batcher.enqueue(panelReq)
planner.coalesce(window=50ms)
merged = planner.mergeQueries(coalesced)
result = db.query(merged.withAuthFilters())
planner.splitAndReturn(result)
```
Maria: Also consider sampling for metrics-heavy panels (e.g., traces, infra metrics). Sampling 1-5% for certain visualization queries can cut cost by ~10x with controlled error. We should expose sampling per-panel in panel config.
Anya: We should formalize SLOs per route: e.g., panel-render p95 <= 300ms, p99 <= 900ms. When planner detects SLO deviation, it flips a degradation policy: serve from cache / increase sampling / return aggregated summary.
Kevin: Circuit breaker idea: maintain per-panel failure budget and open circuit when budget exceeded. While open, route to cached or precomputed. Also add tracing tags so we can see which panels trigger fallbacks.
Maria: Example cache key design: `tenant:panel:id:v{schema_version}:policy_hash:time_bucket`. Keep time_bucket as minute-level for TTL=60s caching. For sensitive panels use time_bucket=5s and stricter encryption flags.
Sam: Rolling plan suggestion: 1) add telemetry + heatmap of queries by panel (2 weeks), 2) implement prototype planner (coalescing + merge) behind feature flag (1 sprint), 3) experiment auth pushdown on non-prod tenants and a small set of customers (2 sprints), 4) canary rollout with infra-bot gating and runtime kill-switch. :rocket:
infra-bot: Deploy window scheduled for canary on 1806120000 — will post canary results.
Anya: Agree with phased plan. Also document operational runbook: how to force-fallback, invalidate caches, and revert planner.
Kevin: I'll take ownership of the auth-invalidation design + tests. Will write a small harness to fuzz policy changes.
Maria: I'll prototype the aggregator cache and sampling knobs; will produce a perf comparison against planner baseline.
Sam: Thanks — I'll draft the RFC follow-up with the plan, signal flows, and required metrics. Opening an RFC PR today and listing owners. If anyone has objections ping me or drop inline comments. :+1:
